lessonDecisions.note: Assessed does-not-apply by delivery-lead with ev:ev-mv1eo87o-01c933d5. The lesson is about a PreToolUse guard that resolves the project root from the harness directory; no task in this plan builds a hook or guard mapping writes to a record (the approved brief and spec name no such component), and the guard that governs this nested record is already the repaired version the lesson names (sha256 d43f4b54..., per-target fileRoot). It matches every task only through shared project words. Operational consequence kept in the plan anyway: every ownership glob is relative to examples/rescuestock and no glob names .eccode/, .claude/ or hooks.

phases.name: B: foundation, data model, planner and oracle
phases.goal: A runnable zero-dependency skeleton on Node >= 22.13 (package.json, flag-free scripts/check-node.cjs gate, config with Secret wrapper, log, clock, db with migrations 001-005, http layer with Host check and security headers, health/config routes, RS-FIX-1 seed), the pure domain (planner + brute-force oracle, money/time/compat/canonical, state tables, rescue-status derivation with its totality property test, explanation templates) and the offline test harness (net guard, node-proc, server-proc, app-harness, p95 report, clean-checkout check).
acceptanceCriteria: RS-06: with RS-FIX-1 and the pinned inventory the planner returns A+B at 8400 cents, 2 pickups, ready 10:30; with A on_hand 2 it returns Ax2 at 7000 cents, 1 pickup; the oracle property test (500 seeded catalogs, <= 6 offers, on_hand 0-3) agrees with the planner on every catalog [D: test/unit/domain/planner-fixture.test.js, planner-oracle.property.test.js]
RS-07: supplier C is rejected with INCOMPATIBLE_LID_DIAMETER [D: planner-fixture]
RS-08: supplier D is rejected with READY_AFTER_DEADLINE [D: planner-fixture]
RS-09: with B at on_hand 0 and, separately, B withdrawn, the best plan is A+E at 9500 cents, 2 pickups, ready 10:40 [D: planner-fixture]

RS-10: B removed and budget 9000: infeasible, blocking includes OVER_BUDGET, A and E carry INSUFFICIENT_QTY and OVER_BUDGET, exactly two relaxations (budget -> 9500 A+E; deadline -> 11:20 D alone 8000, 1 pickup) and no maxPickups relaxation [D: planner-fixture]
RS-11: max pickups 1: infeasible; A, B and E carry exactly INSUFFICIENT_QTY and TOO_MANY_PICKUPS; C and D keep their RS-07/RS-08 codes [D: planner-fixture]

NFR1: package.json has no dependencies, devDependencies only {@playwright/test: 1.56.1}, engines.node >=22.13; every script that passes a flag to node starts with 'node scripts/check-node.cjs &&' (F-TR-4); start-old-node runs the exact start line on /opt/node20 and /opt/node21 and sees a non-zero exit with 'needs Node >= 22.13 (found'; start-health serves GET /api/health 200; scripts/clean-checkout.sh copies the project's tracked and unignored files to an empty directory, runs npm install (npm registry only), npm test (offline, net guard on, no browser) and npm start, and gets /api/health 200 [D + I]

NFR4: config.js reads secrets only from process.env and wraps them in Secret (toString/toJSON/inspect redacted; errors name the variable, never the value); .env.example holds every variable name with placeholders or non-secret defaults only; test/scan/env-example.test.js asserts no real-looking value and that every name config.js reads is listed [D + I]

Prerequisites reviewed in this phase (proved later as RS-36/RS-38): migrations 001-005 match the spec DDL, apply in BEGIN IMMEDIATE with sha256 checksums and are safe when two processes start together; audit_events and inventory_ledger UPDATE/DELETE fail; derive.js implements the revision-2 table row by row (rows 1-14 incl. 4a, 5a) and its totality property test (>= 20,000 seeded walks x 120 events) never reaches row 14 and asserts RS-36 (i)-(iv); states.js tests every allowed and refused pair
npm test passes offline with the net guard active and launches no browser; every test that proves a criterion or finding carries its id at the start of its name

phases.name: C: auth, dashboards, requests, plans, reservations, supplier confirmations, expiry
phases.goal: Server sessions with CSRF, throttles, Host check and default-deny RBAC; customer requests with manual requirement confirmation, planning, approval with hash and total, idempotent BEGIN IMMEDIATE reservations with per-customer caps; supplier order confirm/ready/handover and inventory PATCH; admin reset/faults/timeline/metrics shells; the request view computing the rescue status through derive.js; the three dashboards built against the contract fixtures; multi-process reservation tests and the browser harness.
acceptanceCriteria: RS-12: a plan whose cups or lids total is below the requirement is never produced as feasible, and approve with a tampered planHash or expectedTotalCents returns 409 PLAN_CHANGED (stored plan failing re-validation: PLAN_INVALID) [D: test/api/approve-guards.test.js + planner-fixture]

RS-14: two OS processes (busy_timeout 5000) reserve A's last bundle concurrently on one SQLite file: one reservation active, the other 409 OUT_OF_STOCK, reserved <= on_hand; with busy_timeout 0 and a held write lock reserve answers 503 DB_BUSY with Retry-After [D: test/integration/rs14-two-process-reserve.test.js, rs14-db-busy.test.js]

RS-16: same Idempotency-Key and body -> same reservation id, no second reservation or ledger row; same key with another body -> 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; same key on a second plan -> 422 with no rows, before and after the key row is purged (F-TR-1); a concurrent same-key race resolves to one reservation [D: test/api/reserve-idempotency.test.js]
RS-28: supplier A patching supplier B's inventory gets 403 and nothing changes (whole PATCH refused) [D: test/api/isolation.test.js]
RS-30: customer and supplier sessions calling admin fault and reset routes get 403; unauthenticated 401 [D: test/api/isolation.test.js]

RS-33: browser journey at 360 px and 1280 px: an infeasible request ends on the explanation screen with blocking constraints, per-candidate codes and computed relaxations; no reservation, order or payment operation exists (checked in the database) [B: test/browser/journey-infeasible.test.js, screenshots in test/browser/out/]

RS-36: GET /api/requests/:id computes rescueStatus with derive.js on every read; a schema query finds no column storing a rescue status [D: test/api/rescue-status.test.js, test/api/schema-no-rescue-status.test.js, test/unit/domain/derive.test.js]; [I] reviewer inspects derive.js against the revision-2 table and the view (F-TR-9)

Auth contract (ARCH-25) with SEC-1 (pair/IP hard limits, cross-IP delay only), SEC-9 (username_key normalisation, case variants), SEC-13 (Host allow-list -> 421), SEC-20 (register rotation, no Access-Control-Allow-* header) and SEC-5 (admin password >= 16 chars from env, admin disabled when unset) asserted in test/api/auth.test.js; SEC-2 asserted in test/api/abuse-limits.test.js with the defaults

F-TR-17 resolved by an environment setting: RS_REGISTER_PER_IP_PER_HOUR (default 5; a value above 5 is refused at startup unless RS_TEST_OFFLINE=1); auth.test.js keeps the default and asserts the 6th registration from one IP -> 429 register_ip; the browser and multi-process harnesses set it to 1000 under RS_TEST_OFFLINE=1 together with RS_MAX_REQUESTS_PER_CUSTOMER_PER_DAY=1000 and RS_MAX_LIVE_RESERVATIONS_PER_CUSTOMER=1, so every journey registers its own fresh customer (F-TR-15: fresh database per browser file)

HTTP contract: test/api/contracts.test.js asserts status, envelope, requestId and success-body field types for every route that exists after this phase, against the example responses in test/fixtures/contracts/ that the frontend uses
npm test and npm run test:browser pass

phases.name: D: model extraction with provenance, uploads and retention
phases.goal: Bilingual extraction through the ExtractionProvider contract (deterministic fake for tests; Claude CLI and Anthropic API adapters verified against a recorded transcript and a loopback stub), strict schema validation, grounding and provenance, the degraded manual path, model budget/rate/concurrency controls in integer micro-dollars, image upload by magic bytes with retention and request deletion, the EXT-1 corpus and the opt-in live-model runner, and the matching UI.
acceptanceCriteria: RS-01 [D]: the RS-FIX-1 Arabic and English wordings yield identical core fields (product type, quantities, capacity, diameter, deadline, budget, max pickups) through POST /api/requests/:id/extract with the fake provider [test/api/extract.test.js]
RS-02 [D]: a clear package image yields capacity and diameter with provenance 'image' [test/api/extract-image.test.js]

RS-03 [D + B]: ambiguous images give unknown fields, >= 1 clarification question and no number absent from the image [test/eval/extraction-fake.test.js]; faults timeout, invalid_json, schema_invalid, error, budget refusal and rate refusal give schema_ok=false, an error code, every field unknown, degraded: true [test/api/extract-degraded.test.js]; the request page shows 'Automatic reading unavailable — please enter the details' with a manual field for every core field, and confirming them creates a requirements version with provenance manual and planning proceeds [test/browser/degraded-extraction.test.js]

RS-05 [D]: injection strings in text, image text and catalog text (planted in products.name through a DB fixture, SEC-17) stay data; permissions, amounts, suppliers, plan versions and roles equal the control run; explanations are template text; with rephrasing on, output carrying a number or supplier code absent from the trace is discarded [test/api/injection.test.js, test/unit/ai/rephrase.test.js]

RS-39 [D]: upload accepts only PNG/JPEG/WebP by magic bytes (declared image/png with other bytes -> 415), <= 5 MB (413 above), stored under a random 128-bit name; customer Y uploading to X's request -> 404 with no file written; owner DELETE removes image file and row, raw text and extraction text (409 PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS while money is held; tombstone with settled payments); with a pinned clock the sweep deletes at 7 d + 1 min, keeps at 6 d 23 h and writes an audit event [test/api/uploads-retention.test.js]

NFR6 [D]: every response and log line carries requestId; config inspection shows haiku as the default model; with fake per-call cost 0.10, cap 0.10, RS_MODEL_DAILY_BUDGET_USD=0.25 and RS_MODEL_CUSTOMER_DAILY_SHARE=1 pinned in the test's environment (F-TR-18; the test name and the evidence label say so) the third extract is refused with 503 MODEL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED without invoking the provider and enters the degraded path; the 11th extract or upload by one customer within 10 minutes -> 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After; micro-dollar boundaries (0.30 allowed, 0.299999 refused) hold; a separate SEC-10 case with the production share 0.2 refuses the 5th cap-sized call of one customer with details.scope 'customer' while another customer succeeds [test/api/model-budget-rate.test.js]; the log scan finds no Authorization header value, token, secret, payer data or provider body [test/scan/secrets.test.js]

Live-model parts are not claimed by this phase: npm run test:live-model refuses (exit 2, named message) without RS_LIVE_MODEL=1 [D]; the real-model run over EXT-1 (RS-01/02/03/05 [LM], NFR6 cost report, F-TR-13 schemaAccepted) is the separately listed check LIVE-M1 and stays Unverified until it is run with an authenticated Claude CLI or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and the user's approval of the USD 5 ceiling
ExtractionProvider contract suite (fake, CLI against a stub binary replaying the recorded transcript, Anthropic against a loopback stub) passes [test/unit/ai/provider-contract.test.js]
npm test and npm run test:browser pass

phases.name: E: PayPal payment flow, saga, webhooks and reconciliation
phases.goal: The PaymentProvider contract with a DB-backed fake (faults, PayPal-Request-Id replay model, fake approval listener on a different site with its own CSP) and the Sandbox REST v2 adapter verified against a loopback paypal-stub; the provider call protocol with the sender table; create/return/cancel/abandon with the void rule; the execute claim and captures with lease fencing; the reconciler (stale intents, read-before-resend, pending polls, expiry); verified webhooks; the payment UI; and the two-process execute and browser happy-path journeys.
acceptanceCriteria: RS-04: with budget or deadline missing, POST /api/plans/:id/approve and POST /api/orders/:id/paypal/create return 409 MISSING_BUDGET / MISSING_DEADLINE (budget first) and no reservation or payment operation or provider call is created [D: test/api/approve-guards.test.js, test/api/paypal-create.test.js]

RS-18 [D]: cancel URL leaves the operation created with buyer_cancelled_at (or voided), no capture call or row, execute -> 409; 'Try approval again' and 'Abandon purchase' offered; abandon or expiry voids every other outstanding authorization, releases the reservation, plan non_executable (PAYMENT_CANCELLED or RESERVATION_EXPIRED) [test/api/paypal-cancel.test.js]

RS-19 [D]: client-supplied amount, currency or supplier on every payment route is ignored; the provider request body (fake and Sandbox adapter against paypal-stub) carries the server-approved supplier-order total [test/api/amount-tampering.test.js]

RS-20 [D]: two server processes x 5 concurrent execute: one approved -> executing claim, nine return the current state with no provider call; the fake records exactly N get_authorization + N capture calls and nothing else (F-TR-8), one capture per order with PayPal-Request-Id so:<id>:capture:1; three hits on the return URL give one authorize call [test/integration/rs20-two-process-execute.test.js, test/api/paypal-return-idempotent.test.js]

RS-21 [D]: one DENIED authorization -> no capture on any order, plan non_executable (AUTHORIZATION_FAILED naming the supplier), other authorizations voided, reservation released, the exact buyer message; PENDING -> authorization_pending and execute 409 AUTHORIZATION_PENDING with no capture until the reconciler observes CREATED [test/api/authorization-denied.test.js, test/api/authorization-pending.test.js]

RS-23 [D]: the same webhook transmission id delivered twice applies once; RS-24 [D]: an invalid signature is rejected 4xx, stored with signature_status invalid, no transition; plus SEC-6 (60/min per IP, pre-checks before any provider call) and SEC-16 (merchant, provider and non-archived scoping) [test/api/webhooks.test.js]

RS-25 [D]: a lost capture response leaves the operation unknown; the reconciler reads provider state and then marks captured, capture_pending (polled) or re-sends with the same PayPal-Request-Id; no second capture; an intent left at restart is treated as unknown [test/api/lost-response.test.js]

RS-27 [D]: customer X requesting Y's request or order id gets 404/403 and no data, including /api/paypal/return?token= and /cancel?token= with Y's token (404, no authorize call, no state change) [test/api/isolation.test.js]

RS-31(a) [B]: journey request -> review -> plan -> reservation -> approvals -> supplier confirmations -> capture -> readiness -> collection at 360 px and 1280 px with screenshots, the app on localhost and the fake approval page on 127.0.0.1 (cross-site), each 'Approve (simulated)' landing on /api/paypal/return with the session, one Cancel landing on /api/paypal/cancel, no CSP console message (F-TR-14) [test/browser/journey-happy.test.js]; the listener and paypal-stub send exactly one CSP header equal to approvalPageCsp(appOrigin) [D: test/api/fake-approval-headers.test.js]

Design items asserted: ARCH-22 lost-authorize void hook (test/api/void-rule-lost-authorize.test.js), ARCH-23 claim on stored expiry with the provider read after the claim (test/api/execute.test.js), F-TR-3 sender table and crash_after_return_commit hook implemented, F-TR-11 order presentation, SEC-3 approval-host and base-URL allow-list in the Sandbox adapter, PaymentProvider contract suite on both adapters (test/unit/payments/provider-contract.test.js)

Live PayPal parts are not claimed by this phase: npm run test:live-paypal refuses without RS_LIVE_PAYPAL=1 and credentials; the Sandbox runs (LIVE-P1: RS-18/19/20/23/24 [LP]; LIVE-P2: RS-31(b)/RS-32(b) hosted approval page) need RS_PAYPAL_DEFAULT_CLIENT_ID, RS_PAYPAL_DEFAULT_CLIENT_SECRET, RS_PAYPAL_DEFAULT_WEBHOOK_ID (or per-supplier sets) and network access to api-m.sandbox.paypal.com and www.sandbox.paypal.com, are user-run, and stay Unverified with blocker A6/Q2 until then
npm test and npm run test:browser pass

phases.name: F: replanning, compensation and restart recovery
phases.goal: Supersession on offer and stock changes with the durable re-plan queue, supplier refusal with re-planning that excludes the supplier, expiry voids, capture-failure compensation (voids, refunds, reconciling -> released with restock), lease takeover with epoch and send-token fencing, restart recovery, admin refund_order and forced reset, ledger completeness, the recovery UI, and the restart, takeover and replacement-journey tests.
acceptanceCriteria: RS-13 [D]: a price change of an offer used by an approved plan (order not confirmed, plan not executing) supersedes it, recomputes a new proposed version, reserve/execute on the old one -> 409 PLAN_SUPERSEDED, every old authorization voided (one void call each), reservation released (one ledger row per item), orders cancelled, 'Prices changed: review plan vN' shown; after the supplier confirmed or after the claim the plan is not superseded [test/api/supersession.test.js]

RS-15 [D]: an expired reservation is released exactly once (inventory back, one expire ledger row, second pass no-op); an expiry pass after the claim and before the first capture changes nothing; expiry before execute voids every authorization, plan non_executable (RESERVATION_EXPIRED) and the request shows 'Reservation expired — no money was taken; re-plan with current stock' [test/api/reservation-expiry.test.js]

RS-17 [D + B]: refusal before the claim -> order refused, outstanding authorizations voided, reservation released, plan non_executable (SUPPLIER_REFUSED), status cancelling while a void is outstanding, refusal reason with 'Review the new plan', new version computed without that supplier [test/api/supplier-refusal.test.js; test/browser/refusal.test.js]

RS-22 [D]: capture failing on the second supplier refunds the first capture and voids the rest; refund_requested -> refund_pending -> refunded|refund_failed; plan non_executable (CAPTURE_FAILED); reservation reconciling until every refund and void completes, then released with restock rows (refund_failed keeps reconciling and failed_needs_attention); handover 409 HANDOVER_BLOCKED; a PENDING capture blocks handover and the next capture, and lease_epoch does not grow across reconciler ticks while it is pending (F-TR-7) [test/api/capture-compensation.test.js]

RS-26 [D]: SIGKILL mid-saga and restart keeps orders, operations, provider calls and recovery progress; after the lease expires the reconciler takes over and completes the saga; lease-takeover variants A and B (ARCH-26) give exactly one non-replayed capture per order; return-crash cases (a), (b), (c) (F-TR-3) [test/integration/rs26-restart.test.js, lease-takeover.test.js, return-crash.test.js]

RS-32(a) [B]: B's offer withdrawn by the admin stock-depletion fault before B confirms; the buyer approves the 9500-cent A+E plan; the old plan superseded, its authorizations voided, B's order cancelled; the replacement flow completes through collection with the cross-site approval round-trip assertion [test/browser/journey-replacement.test.js]

RS-37 [D]: admin reset returns 409 RESET_BLOCKED while any operation is approved|authorization_pending|authorized|capture_pending|captured|refund_requested|refund_pending|unknown; forced reset requires a reason, voids authorized operations and runs one bounded read-resolve pass, lists stranded operations (SEC-11), and archives rather than deletes operations and provider calls [test/api/admin-reset.test.js]

RS-38 [D]: any UPDATE or DELETE on audit_events or inventory_ledger fails; every reserve, release, expire, consume and restock writes a ledger row, and for every product the ledger sums equal on_hand and reserved [test/api/ledgers.test.js]

Design items asserted: F-TR-2 re-plan queue never drops an entry and backs off (test/api/replan-queue.test.js); F-TR-6 capture landing after the void intent ends refunded with one capture, one void attempt and one refund call (test/api/void-capture-race.test.js)
npm test and npm run test:browser pass

phases.name: G: final verification, clean checkout, browser UX, labels and submission materials
phases.goal: Accessibility and all UI states, labelling for both payment adapters, the six-answer request page, the full secrets scan over assets, responses, logs, screenshots and submission files, live-suite refusals, performance budgets, final README with runbooks and operator notes, submission materials, a clean-checkout run on the final tree, and the project evidence table that the verification report cites.
acceptanceCriteria: RS-29 [D + I]: a scan of built frontend assets, recorded API responses, logs, browser screenshots and submission files finds no client id or secret value; config redacts secrets in errors [test/scan/secrets.test.js]

RS-34 [D + B]: fake adapter payloads (payments and extraction) carry simulated: true and the UI shows the 'Simulated' badge and the persistent banner; Sandbox adapter payloads carry provider 'paypal-sandbox' and sandbox: true and every payment element shows 'PayPal Sandbox — no real money'; seeded data carries demo: true with the 'Demo data' badge and 'Test prices, not market prices'; with the Sandbox adapter against the loopback stub under RS_TEST_OFFLINE=1, labels.testMode and the 'Test mode — local stubs, nothing is real' banner (SEC-3); config refuses any PayPal base URL other than the Sandbox host or a loopback stub in test mode [test/api/labelling.test.js, test/unit/config/hosts.test.js, test/browser/labelling.test.js]

RS-35 [B + I]: the request page answers all six questions (requirements with provenance, decision trace, rejections, cents totals, offer vs commitment, compensation state and next step) with text rendered from planner codes [test/browser/six-questions.test.js]

NFR2 [B]: at 360 px and 1280 px keyboard-only completion of the happy path (with the approval round-trip assertion), visible focus, labelled controls, text status indicators, and the loading, empty, error, retry, timeout, expired-reservation and degraded-extraction states rendered [test/browser/a11y-states.test.js]

NFR3 [D + I]: npm test, npm run test:browser, npm run test:live-model and npm run test:live-paypal are separate scripts; both live scripts refuse without their flag [test/scan/live-refusal.test.js]; live reports are labelled with suite, provider, model or merchant mode and corpus version (inspection of the runners)

NFR5 [D]: planner < 1 s on RS-FIX-1 and on each of the 200 seeded generator catalogs [test/timing/planner-generator.test.js]; p95 over the deterministic API test calls < 300 ms and suite time < 5 min as reported by scripts/report-p95.js

Final tree: scripts/clean-checkout.sh passes (NFR1 re-check); README documents install, seed, start, tests, the one-time npx playwright install chromium, demo accounts (SEC-5), the operator note for retakes (F-TR-15), RS_REGISTER_PER_IP_PER_HOUR (F-TR-17), live runbooks with the env var names and the allow-list, retention, labelling, the Node floor and Q9 branch, MIT licence

docs/evidence-table.md lists all 45 criteria with suite, test names and evidence ids; every live row (LIVE-M1, LIVE-P1, LIVE-P2) is marked Unverified with its blocker; RS-20/RS-26 Sandbox rows say they rest on the fake's model of PayPal until the live run (SEC-18); single-credential weakened rows are labelled (A2); the NFR6 row states RS_MODEL_CUSTOMER_DAILY_SHARE=1 (F-TR-18)
Full regression on the final tree: npm test and npm run test:browser pass

acceptanceCriteria: Execute: the spec's check order on stored data only, conditional approved -> executing UPDATE with executor_id, lease_epoch + 1 and lease_until inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, no provider call before or inside it; losers get 200 with the current state; the winner consumes the reservation (consume ledger rows) and queues so:<id>:capture:1 per order (ARCH-23) [execute.test.js]

Post-claim authorization read under the fence, then sequential captures in supplier-code order with start/record under G(now); step 3 pauses without a send on capture_pending or unknown (F-TR-7 first half); all captured -> executed; lease >= 3 x timeout enforced by config

Reconciler tick in order: stale intents -> unknown, resolve unknown by reading first (protocol §6), poll pending, expire reservations, take over executing plans whose lease lapsed (completed in phase F), send queued authorize/void/refund per the sender table, release check, drain the re-plan queue through supersession.js, housekeeping incl. purge of invalid/unverified webhook rows older than 7 days (SEC-6) and stale reserved model-spend rows

RS-25 lost capture response cases, RS-21 PENDING case (execute 409 AUTHORIZATION_PENDING until the reconciler sees CREATED), ARCH-22 lost-authorize test (exactly one void after supersession and reconcile, plus the row-2 escalation clause)
main.js starts the fake approval listener (fake provider only) and the reconciler at startup and every RS_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS

tasks.title: Capture-failure compensation with refunds and restock, lease takeover with epoch and send-token fencing, admin refund_order and forced reset, ledger completeness
acceptanceCriteria: Compensation (step 5) in one transaction under the fence: plan non_executable (CAPTURE_FAILED | AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED), reservation consumed -> reconciling, queued captures cancelled, authorized -> void, captured -> refund_requested + so:<id>:refund:1; refund results to refunded / refund_pending (polled) / refund_failed (escalation); release check -> released with restock rows only when nothing is outstanding

Takeover (step 6): epoch + 1 inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE only when lease_until <= now and no operation is capture_pending or unknown (F-TR-7); every open capture call resolved by reading before any send; re-send only with the same PayPal-Request-Id; late result writes fenced by epoch and send_token (saga.lease_lost logged)
F-TR-6: a rejected void whose read shows CAPTURED moves the operation to captured and queues the refund in the same transaction

Admin refund_order only for captured operations of executed plans; forced reset per SEC-11 (void authorized, bounded 30 s read-resolve pass, stranded list in response and audit); reset archives operations and provider calls, never deletes

RS-22 (incl. PENDING capture with lease_epoch constant across ticks), RS-37, RS-38 (every reserve, release, expire, consume and restock writes a ledger row; per-product ledger sums equal on_hand and reserved) tests named with their ids
